The Crew Motorfest is a big step forward for the series and easily the best Crew game so far. The map of Oʻahu is beautiful and packed with detail, making just driving around feel fun and relaxing. The playlist system is a great idea, offering themed events that don’t feel repetitive and help the game stay engaging.

It has a more lively feel than Forza Horizon 5 (long time Forza player). Car handling and physics feel more arcade but easy to control with a Logitech G923 wheel (preferred), even on default settings. Cars tend to snap oversteer easily regardless of front/rear/AWD if you aggressively turn at high speeds - realistic but too sensitive. this can be dialed in through steering assist/sensitivity in settings. It has variety of vehicles from cars, motorcycles, boats and even planes, though I mostly stick with cars. You can progress through "Playlists" and earn reward cars, are engaging and unique for each theme. Example: "Vintage Playlist" using cars from 50s, 60s. 70s, and 80s restricts use of GPS and driving aids; in place, relies on vignetted photographs of landmarks in the game for navigation - a nice old school touch! You can also set custom playlists using your car of choice (haven't tried that yet... too busy completing on preset playlists!). My favorite so far is the RedBull Playlist because of fast-paced and the challenge of driving variety of speed machines from rally car, F1, motorcycle, and a plane! This game does require a fast computer with 8+ CPU cores and a GPU with 8-16GB VRAM. I can run it smoothly at 1440p - 60fps installed on a computer with 12-core Ryzen 9 7900 CPU and Radeon RX 7800XT GPU. 32GB RAM is highly recommended.

I'm a pretty bad driver (in video games). I don't have a fancy setup with a wheel, and I don't really follow racing IRL so usually I skip out on these games.

But recently I had some racing itch that desperately needed to be scratched and this was on sale. So I went for it. And WOW. It's been a while since I last played a racing game (I think it was Xbox One Forza?) and I can't deny that this is very, very fun. I turn the difficulty settings down until I'm comfortable and slightly challenged and just drive. 

I have a super ultrawide monitor and a beefy PC so the graphics are set to ultra settings. It looks lifelike. And with a PS5 controller, the haptic feedback is unparalleled. 

There are lots of different events and race varieties, so I can't see myself getting bored. I particularly like the Drift sequences. More cars than I can ever "purchase" and they have my favorites. 

Big downside - it's online only (even if you play by yourself). Like, I don't get that. I know people IRL (IYKYK) that will instantly turn away from a game if it has this setting. I sorta get it.
